children: Chicago soybean futures eased on Friday after notching all-time highs in the last session amid China's purchase of U.S. beans before the upcoming meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
The most-traded soybeans on the Chicago Board of Trade
fell 1.1% to $13.17 a bushel by 1045 GMT. CBOT wheat
dropped 0.8% at $7.35-1/2 a bushel, while corn
Soybean futures jumped to their highest in three years in the previous session supported by Chinese demand.

China has bought around 1 million metric tons of U.S. soybeans this week, traders told Reuters, as the world's top oilseed buyer steps up purchases ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington later this month.
The purchases take China's total U.S. soybean buying to nearly half of the 25 million tons the White House said Beijing had committed to annually through 2028.
On grains, the run-up to the USDA supply and demand forecasts on Friday encouraged profit-taking by investors, who have built up a large long position in wheat.

The USDA's forecasts on Friday are expected to indicate the extent to which hot, dry spells this summer hurt U.S. Midwest crops. Market participants also continue to monitor Black Sea tensions and grain export disruption in the key grain production region.

Renewed diplomatic moves to end Russia's war with Ukraine have weighed on prices, though more Russian attacks on Thursday, including one on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro that damaged a vegetable oil factory of U.S. agrifood group Bunge
, kept attention on continuing disruption to the massive Black Sea grain trade.
Commzerbank raised its year-end wheat price forecasts, citing the ongoing attacks by Russia and Ukraine on each other's ports.

at €240 per ton, up from €220 previously.
